reasons: The rule applies: Section 3.4 gives HDI (the host/vendor counterparty) inspection rights over the Company's (our party's) payment-calculation records, so it is an audit right binding Customer.

The clause is a genuine deviation, not an acceptable fallback: it is entirely silent on frequency, which under the playbook leaves an unlimited/repeated inspection right — expressly walk-away territory — while the fallback requires at least a once-per-year cap.

The redline is the smallest edit that reaches the position: it inserts only 'not more than once in any twelve (12) month period' into the existing sentence, leaving the already-favourable 30-day notice, business-hours, cost-borne-by-HDI and records-only (no system access) terms untouched.

The comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, correctly states what changed and why, and does not misdescribe the existing terms; the non-independent auditor point is properly noted as a sub-element rather than redlined.
Deterministic checks are consistent (frequency limit added, edit ratio reflects an insertion into a short paragraph rather than a rewrite).
